claims.text: OpenShell is intended as a policy-controlled runtime for autonomous AI agents; this PoC did not validate its security boundaries.
The pinned README describes file, system-call and network controls plus formal policy verification as intended capabilities, not observed results.
PoC question: can fresh UBI source builds run under OpenShift restricted-v2 and provide a usable sandbox lifecycle through the pinned SDK?
The operator-supplied pinned README capture shows source context, not runtime behavior.
Five original terminal checks were recorded once; this account does not replay tests.
Gateway readiness and mTLS access
Observe ready workloads; require certificate-authenticated API success and rejection without a client certificate.
PASS: ready workloads; authenticated Health and ListSandboxes succeeded; ListSandboxes without a client certificate returned UNAUTHENTICATED.
Sandbox readiness and process contract
Create a READY sandbox; verify stdout, stderr, deliberate exit 7, non-root UID and requested placement.
ERROR: one CreateSandbox call returned grpc_failed_precondition, gRPC 9, because no shared supervisor was attached; process checks did not complete.
Persistent workspace lifecycle
Write a marker, stop/start the sandbox and require exact readback with unchanged sandbox identity.
SKIP: process_dependency_failed; marker persistence and restart behavior were not tested.
Scoped reachable-control network contrast
Compare worker-to-gateway metrics reachability with sandbox TCP port 2222; this is not a policy-enforcement test.
SKIP: sandbox_not_created; the planned reachability contrast produced no result and proves no enforcement boundary.
Run-owned sandbox deletion
Delete only the run-owned sandbox; verify SDK and Kubernetes object disappearance, not PVC reclamation.
SKIP: sandbox_not_created; no usable sandbox existed for the planned deletion contract.
Gateway and supervisor were Ready under restricted-v2; readiness did not establish supervisor attachment or sandbox execution.
Gateway mounted a Bound 10Gi data PVC on the specified worker; this was not a validated persistent sandbox workspace.
Observed setup: PoC worker/pinned SDK, gateway, shared supervisor and gateway data PVC; assignment was missing, not a healthy connection.
The gateway-topology create path stopped at the missing shared-supervisor assignment; no usable sandbox or persistent workspace was created.
All three pinned-source UBI builds completed and pushed: gateway, supervisor and sandbox; zero build retries.
The full-feature gateway build included openshell-prover and vendored Z3; no standalone prover execution or formal-verification behavior was validated.
Operator assistance included same-revision Dockerfile designs, branch-protection attestation and a source screenshot; none establishes independent validation.
Existing prerequisites, service account and node guidance were adopted; capacity, isolation prerequisites and unattended reproducibility were not independently qualified.
A transient Sandbox CR was rolled back after assignment failed; default workspace metadata and intermediate creation logs were not lifecycle success.
Later curl diagnostics verified TLS and token acceptance on an empty Attach request, then returned gRPC 3 before hello; they did not establish Rust attachment.
Source inspection found shorthand logging discarded structured error fields; the generic attachment warning hid the underlying error.
The Rust supervisor attachment root cause remains unknown; TLS, token, network policy, product defect and platform incompatibility are not established causes.
Original totals: 1 pass, 0 fail, 1 error, 3 skip, 0 incomplete; five terminal records, not five successful checks.
Source-build feasibility, workload readiness and narrow mTLS behavior were demonstrated; the usable SDK-driven sandbox lifecycle objective was not achieved.
Later diagnostics neither change the five original outcomes nor add a sixth scenario; execution accounting is complete despite the blocked objective.
Evidence gap: missing_trace. Retained logs and action observations are not a complete distributed trace.
Policy boundaries remain unknown, not a demonstrated product failure; port reachability, NetworkPolicy presence and readiness do not prove enforcement.
No production qualification, Kubernetes portability or OpenShift AI integration/certification was established; GPU, HA, load and isolation validation were excluded.
Blog ineligible; cloud publication blocked and outside authorization. The prior Drive refresh failed and was not retried; prepared inputs are not rendered artifacts.
Investigate the real Rust Attach handshake with separately authorized, sanitized error context; establish hello, pool membership and a sustained assignment stream.
After attachment and explicit execution authorization, capture future process, workspace, scoped network and deletion checks as new attempts; preserve these original outcomes.
Do not weaken TLS or expand RBAC based on an assumed cause; retain source/image identities and assistance disclosures, and require separate cloud authorization.

slides.title: OpenShell: runtime intent and the lifecycle question

narration.text: OpenShell is intended to run autonomous AI agents under declared policy controls.
Its pinned README describes controls for file access, system calls and network connections.
It also describes formal checks of policy changes before they are applied.
These are project design claims, not security results from this run.
The PoC asked whether fresh UBI builds could run under OpenShift restricted-v2 and support a usable sandbox lifecycle.
The intended client path used the SDK from the pinned source revision.
The supplied README image gives source context, not a view of a working application.

slides.title: Access passed; sandbox creation returned an error

narration.text: The access check tested workload readiness and mutual TLS, using client certificates for authenticated API calls.
It passed: both workloads were ready, and authenticated Health and ListSandboxes calls succeeded.
ListSandboxes without a client certificate returned UNAUTHENTICATED, so the negative control also behaved as required.
Health alone was not used as the authentication rejection test.
The process check aimed to create a ready sandbox and verify output, deliberate exit seven, non-root identity and placement.
Its single CreateSandbox call returned gRPC status nine, recorded as a failed precondition error.
No shared supervisor was attached to the gateway, so the planned process checks did not complete.
These are original recorded outcomes, not checks replayed for this presentation.

slides.title: Three dependent checks were skipped, not passed

narration.text: The workspace check would write a marker, stop and restart the sandbox, then verify its identity and marker.
It was skipped because the process dependency failed, so persistence and restart behavior were not tested.
The network check planned a gateway metrics reachability control followed by a connection attempt to sandbox port twenty-two twenty-two.
It was skipped because no usable sandbox was created, so the planned contrast produced no result.
Even a completed port contrast would not prove policy enforcement.
The cleanup check would verify deletion of only the run-owned sandbox through the SDK and Kubernetes objects.
It was skipped because no usable sandbox existed for that deletion contract.
Logical disappearance would not establish storage reclamation.

slides.title: Ready components did not supply an attached supervisor

narration.text: The observed setup contained the PoC worker, gateway, shared supervisor and gateway data volume.
The worker used the pinned SDK to reach the gateway, where the API access controls passed.
The gateway and supervisor were ready under restricted-v2, but that did not establish application-level attachment.
The gateway mounted a bound ten-gibibyte data volume on the specified worker.
That volume was not the persistent sandbox workspace planned for lifecycle validation.
The stopped red path marks the missing assignment dependency, not successful traffic between gateway and supervisor.
No usable sandbox or validated persistent workspace appears in this observed topology.

slides.title: Fresh builds completed, with disclosed operator assistance

narration.text: All three components were freshly built from the pinned revision with UBI final images.
The gateway, supervisor and sandbox builds completed and pushed with no build retries.
The full-feature gateway build included the prover and vendored Z3, but compilation did not execute a proof.
The operator supplied same-revision Dockerfile designs that were adapted to build fresh Rust binaries.
The worker adopted the operator's branch-protection attestation rather than independently verifying repository administration settings.
The operator also supplied the source screenshot, existing prerequisites, service account and node guidance.
This run did not independently qualify capacity, underlying isolation prerequisites or fully unattended reproducibility.

slides.title: Attachment remained blocked; later curl did not fix it

narration.text: The gateway briefly created a Sandbox resource, then rolled it back when supervisor assignment failed.
That intermediate message and default workspace metadata did not establish a usable sandbox or persistent workspace.
Later curl diagnostics from the supervisor verified TLS reachability, but the GET response was not a health success.
An empty Attach request accepted the token and reached protocol handling, then returned status three before hello.
This did not establish the Rust client's attachment, pool registration or sustained assignment stream.
Source inspection found that shorthand logging discarded the structured error fields needed to explain the warning.
The root cause remains unknown, and no concrete safe correction was established.
These later diagnostics do not change any original scenario result.

slides.title: Build and access evidence survived a blocked lifecycle

narration.text: The final recorded totals are one pass, zero failures, one error, three skips and zero incomplete records.
Zero failures does not mean success, because the operational error blocked the lifecycle and caused dependent skips.
The positive result is narrower: source builds completed, workloads were ready, and the tested mTLS API behavior worked.
The central objective of a usable SDK-driven sandbox lifecycle was not achieved.
Execution accounting is complete because all five terminal records exist, not because all checks passed.
Later setup diagnostics are context, not a sixth scenario or replacement evidence.

slides.title: Unknown policy boundaries are not a failed security verdict

narration.text: The evidence index retains the missing trace gap, so these logs are not a complete distributed trace.
The intended policy boundaries remain unknown here, rather than demonstrated product failures.
Port reachability and the presence of a NetworkPolicy object do not establish enforcement.
This run did not qualify production use, Kubernetes portability or OpenShift AI integration or certification.
GPU execution, high availability, load and isolation validation were outside scope.
The blog remained ineligible, and cloud publication remained blocked outside authorization.
The prior Drive refresh failed and was not retried.
Prepared presentation inputs do not mean a presentation, video or cloud artifact has been produced.

slides.title: Investigate the real Attach handshake before lifecycle work

narration.text: Investigate the Rust supervisor's real Attach handshake under separate authorization, using narrowly scoped and sanitized error context.
Establish the hello exchange, pool membership and sustained assignment stream before another lifecycle attempt.
Do not weaken TLS or expand permissions based on an assumed cause.
After attachment works and execution is authorized, record the remaining lifecycle checks as new attempts.
Keep the original error and skips, and do not rerun tests merely to improve presentation evidence.
Retain the source revision, immutable image identities and operator-assistance disclosures for future work.
Keep the blog ineligible and seek explicit cloud authorization before any refresh or upload.
